comment: Show the minimap in the top-right corner.
Minimap edge length in screen pixels.
How many blocks one minimap pixel covers. 1 is the finest (1 pixel per block).
Show the biome name under the minimap.
Show the current in-game time under the minimap.
Show the coordinate line under the minimap.
Minimap text alignment: 0 = left edge, 1 = centre, 2 = right edge.
Minimap text size as a percentage of the system GUI scale. 100 and 200 stay pixel-crisp.
World-map view width in blocks at zoom 1x. Mouse wheel changes zoom in game.
Map UI scale: 0 = follow the system GUI scale, 1-4 = fixed scale for the world-map chrome.
Sharpening applied to zoomed-out map tiles (0 = off, 100 = strongest).
Zooming out averages blocks into one pixel; this restores local contrast.
Strength of the north-west relief shading (0 = off, 100 = default, 200 = strongest).
Terrain rising towards the north-west is brightened, terrain falling away is darkened.
Uses heights already stored in the map tiles, so explored areas shade without re-capturing.
Hovering the world map shows block name, biome and coordinates.
Only loaded chunks are queried; unknown areas show nothing.
Show predicted biomes for unexplored areas (built-in, limited to the configured radius).
Prediction is drawn dimmed; real explored terrain always wins.
When hovering an unloaded area, show the predicted biome instead of nothing.
Requires showBiomePrediction.
Draw a darker outline between different predicted biomes (jelly-block look).
When entering a new world whose seed matches an existing map, ask whether to inherit it.
Inheritance copies the old map into this world; the two stay independent.

values.comment: Play a sound when another player's marker arrives.

comment: Show structure locations on the world map.
Positions are computed by the server; no chunks are generated.
Hide the structure overlay when one canvas pixel covers more blocks than this.
Zoom in past this value to see structures; larger values are denser.
false: fixed 110-degree window, 15-degree ticks (default).
true:  the bar spans your field of view, so tick spacing simulates real angles.

values.comment: true: show only the current bearing number (hide bar/ticks).
true: taller bar; false: normal/thin bar (default).

comment: Compass bar width in screen pixels, also capped by the screen width.
Drag the corner grip in the HUD layout editor to change it.

values.comment: true: frosted black background (default); false: no background.

comment: 0: perspective - follow game FOV with tan projection (matches on-screen direction).
1: center only - fixed reference FOV with adjustable spread.
2: linear - fixed 110 degree window (legacy).
Horizontal spread when alignMode=1. Center stays aligned; larger = ticks spread out.

values.comment: Size of marker symbols on the compass bar. 1.0 = original size.

comment: 0: no text effect, 1: vanilla shadow (default), 2: four-way outline.
Outline uses translucent dark grey, not a solid black border.

values.comment: Share markers between players. Turn off for public servers.
Also show markers from other dimensions.
Only share markers within this radius in blocks. 0 = unlimited.

comment: How long a temporary marker (ping / item / entity / container) stays visible.
Marking the same target again refreshes this timer.

values.comment: A death marker disappears after its owner gets this close (blocks).

comment: Answer structure-map queries from players.
Positions come from worldgen placement maths only; no chunks are generated.
Skip structure sets placed closer together than this (in chunks).
Buried treasures, mineshafts and nether fossils use spacing 1-2 and are ~100x denser.

values.comment: Upper bound on structure candidates returned per map cell.
Soft time budget for one map cell scan; the result is marked truncated when exceeded.

comment: Drop candidates whose biome cannot host that structure.
Sampled without generating chunks; turning this off brings back most false positives.
Also list structure sets from other namespaces (mods / datapacks).
They use the same placement maths but their icons and names are not verified yet.
Share explored map tiles between players on a dedicated server or a LAN-published world.
Tiles are stored under <world>/map_pack_tiles; the newest upload wins.

values.comment: Outbound tile bandwidth cap per player, in KiB/s.

comment: Chunks around each player that count as explored; biome and structure predictions only show there.
The union is kept per dimension and survives restarts. 0 disables the limit entirely.
0: off - no sampling at all.
1: 4-block cells (finest; 44 us per chunk, 181 ms per 1024x1024 tile on one thread).
2: 8-block cells (10 us per chunk).
3: 16-block cells (coarsest; 2.8 us per chunk).
On the server this is the minimum step sent to clients; on the client it only toggles the layer (0 = off).
The actual step also grows when radiusBlocks needs more than maxCellsPerAxis samples per axis.
Sampling always runs on a background pool at low priority and pauses itself when the server tick gets slow.
Biome prediction radius in blocks, measured as a circle from the request centre.
1024 matches the default 1024-block fullscreen map and the default reveal radius (64 chunks).
Larger radii coarsen the grid to fit maxCellsPerAxis; anything outside the circle stays blank.
Upper bound on samples per axis for one region.
Default 513 with radiusBlocks 1024 gives 4-block cells.
Lower values coarsen the grid; larger radii also coarsen it automatically.
Store received biome regions on disk per world.
Revisiting an area (or reopening the world) reuses them instead of asking the server again.
